issues.body: evaluate() uses one `seen` set for both newly added suite directories and newly added ids. When a PR adds `bench/foo/...` and also adds id `foo` to `bench/benchmarks.toml`, the T2 suite check runs first and records label `foo` without a `new_id`; the later T1 check calls `check(..., new_id="foo")` but returns immediately because `foo` is already in `seen`. Consequently the `new_id in trunk_ids` violation is never emitted. This defeats rule (c) for the most common new-benchmark change and allows continued edits to the shared append point.
issues.fix_hint: Evaluate fragment placement independently of label de-duplication, or associate each added suite with its matching new id and pass that id during the first check. Add a regression test supplying both `added=["bench/beta/run.sh"]` and a new trunk id `beta`, asserting that exactly one violation is returned and that it contains the fragment-placement reason.
issues.title: Suite de-duplication skips the trunk-append enforcement for normal new suites

verdict.summary: The assembler and its validation tests are generally well scoped, but the new G3 fragment-placement rule is bypassed in the ordinary case where a PR adds both a new bench directory and its matching benchmark id. The de-duplication happens before the new-id-specific placement check, so an entry appended to the shared trunk can pass despite the stated hard invariant. The tests cover a new id in isolation but not the combined T1+T2 path.
